etymology.text: Ideogram: a short stroke above a long one (the mirror of 下). From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *tVŋ ‘top’.

funFacts: 上 and 下 are mirror images: a mark above or below a line.
pitfalls: 上 comes AFTER the noun: 桌子上 ‘on the table’ — never *在上桌子.
在 opens the phrase, 上 closes it: 在 + noun + 上. 上 alone cannot stand after 在 (*书在上) — then use 上面.
subtleties: 上 is also ‘on’ for surfaces that are not on top: 墙上 ‘on the wall’, 街上 ‘in the street’.
After a noun it is usually said lightly: 桌子上 zhuōzi shang.

etymology.text: Traditional 裡 / 裏: semantic 衣 ‘clothes’ + phonetic 里 — the lining of a garment. Simplified Chinese writes it with 里 ‘village; li (mile)’.

funFacts: The traditional 裡 / 裏 contains 衣 ‘clothes’: the first ‘inside’ was the lining of a garment.
pitfalls: An ordinary noun needs 里 to become a place: 在冰箱里 — *在冰箱 is incomplete. Place names and institutions do not: 在北京, 在学校.
里 alone cannot follow 在: *他在里 — use 里面.
subtleties: After a noun 里 is usually toneless: 家里 jiāli.
With rooms and buildings 里 is optional: 在厨房 / 在厨房里.

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辶 ‘walk’ + phonetic 斤.

subtleties: ‘In the garden’ is 在花园里, with 里.

contrasts.value: the yard or courtyard of a house

override.meaning: Wiktionary glosses 院子 ‘(colloquial) courtyard’ — the yard of a house, which is the home’s garden in everyday Mandarin; 花园 is the planted flower garden.

profile.feeling: The yard of a house — chickens, a tree, children playing.

senses.def: yard, courtyard (the garden of a house)

examples.tr: The children are in the yard.

examples.text: 我爷爷家有一个大院子。
examples.py: Wǒ yéye jiā yǒu yí ge dà yuànzi.
examples.tr: My grandfather’s house has a big yard.

examples.py: Yuànzi li yǒu hěn duō huā.
examples.tr: There are lots of flowers in the yard.

etymology.text: 院 ‘courtyard’ (semantic 阝 + phonetic 完) + the noun suffix 子.

funFacts: A Beijing 四合院 is a house with four wings around one courtyard.
pitfalls: In 医院 ‘hospital’ and 学院 ‘college’ 院 means ‘institution’, not ‘yard’.
subtleties: In the countryside the family garden is the 院子; 花园 sounds more like a planted, decorative garden.

profile.feeling: Wooden boards or tiles under your feet.

examples.tr: The cup is on the floor.
The floor is very clean.

examples.text: 我们家的地板是木头的。
examples.py: Wǒmen jiā de dìbǎn shì mùtou de.
examples.tr: Our floors are wooden.

synonyms.nuance: dì: the ground, the floor — 在地上 ‘on the floor / on the ground’

etymology.text: 地 ‘ground, earth’ + 板 ‘board’.

funFacts: Everyday speech often just says 地上 ‘on the ground’: 别坐在地上 ‘don’t sit on the floor’.
pitfalls: ‘On the floor’ needs 上: 在地板上 / 在地上.
‘Floor’ as a storey is not 地板: ‘the third floor’ is 三楼 or 三层.
subtleties: A single board or tile is counted 一块地板.

override.measure: Wiktionary lists 部 for 楼梯 (and Cantonese 条); in everyday Mandarin 这个楼梯 / 一个楼梯 is the usual form, and 个 is never drilled as wrong.

profile.feeling: Up and down between the floors.

examples.tr: The stairs are next to the kitchen.
Let’s take the stairs.
This staircase is very narrow.

synonyms.nuance: diàntī: lift, elevator — not stairs: ‘electric ladder’

etymology.text: 楼 ‘storey, building’ + 梯 ‘ladder’.

funFacts: 楼梯 is a ‘building ladder’, 电梯 an ‘electric ladder’ — the lift.
pitfalls: 楼 means a building or a storey: 楼上 ‘upstairs’, 楼下 ‘downstairs’.
subtleties: In some dialects 楼梯 also means a ladder.

profile.feeling: Shelves and racks — books, cups, everything in its place.

examples.tr: The books are on the shelf.

examples.py: Jiàzi shang yǒu hěn duō bēizi.
examples.tr: There are lots of cups on the shelf.
He doesn’t put on any airs.

phrases.meaning: to put on airs, to act important

etymology.text: 架 ‘frame, rack’ + the noun suffix 子.

funFacts: A person with 架子 ‘a frame’ holds himself stiffly — he puts on airs.
pitfalls: 架子 is any rack or frame; a bookshelf is 书架.
subtleties: ‘On the shelf’ is 架子上, with 上.

override.measure: Wiktionary lists only 组 for 沙发; 张 (one sofa), 套 (a suite) and 个 are standard Mandarin measure words for it, and 张 must not be drilled as wrong.

profile.feeling: Comfort after work — tea, TV, family.

senses.def: (internet slang) the first reply in a forum thread

examples.tr: The sofa is in the living room.
He is sleeping on the sofa.
First reply!

synonyms.nuance: cháng shāfā: couch, settee (a long sofa)

etymology.text: Borrowed from English sofa, probably via Shanghainese.

funFacts: The word travelled far: Arabic صُفَّة ṣuffa ‘bench’ → Turkish sofa → English sofa (Greek σοφάς, German Sofa) → Chinese 沙发.
pitfalls: 沙发 is a sound loan: 沙 ‘sand’ and 发 ‘to send’ carry no meaning here.
subtleties: ‘On the sofa’ is 沙发上: 坐在沙发上.

override.meaning: Wiktionary glosses 冰箱 ‘refrigerator’ — the same as ‘fridge’; the tool compares whole words.

profile.feeling: The humming box of cold drinks and leftovers.

examples.tr: The milk is in the fridge.
There’s nothing in the fridge.

examples.py: Wǒmen mǎi le yì tái xīn bīngxiāng.
examples.tr: We bought a new fridge.

etymology.text: 冰 ‘ice’ + 箱 ‘box, chest’.

funFacts: 冰箱 is an ‘ice box’, like the old English icebox; Cantonese says 雪柜 ‘snow cabinet’.
pitfalls: ‘In the fridge’ is 冰箱里 — the 里 is required.
subtleties: 台 is the measure word for machines: 一台冰箱, 一台电脑.
